_notes: The label space lives in src/sage_shift/labelspace.py; `six_classes` repeats it so a test can check that both agree.
`expected_counts` come from the data audit and the official HyperKvasir split file; scripts/03_build_manifests.py stops if the files disagree.
`paper_table6` is the SAGE paper's Table 6 (arXiv:2606.22144v2, p8): weighted F1 on each model's own test set and on SAGE.
Manifests, features and per-image predictions are never committed: on Colab pass a private Google Drive folder as --out-dir; locally they go to outputs/ (git-ignored).
`preprocessing` values were chosen from aggregate pixel statistics of the SAGE frames before any features were extracted (scripts/05_check_fov.py).

The window settings and the per-dataset `fallback` were added after checking the HyperKvasir sheets, before any fov or colour features were extracted. Green windows (the ScopeGuide thumbnail) cover 3-13% of the frame in HyperKvasir and at most 1.1% in SAGE. HyperKvasir notches come from the black picture-in-picture window of its older processor, which must stay outside the field, so HyperKvasir frames keep their own detection.

image.resize: squash whole frame (as the SAGE authors)

colour.method: Reinhard et al. (2001) mean and SD transfer
colour.statistics: pixels inside the field only; pixels outside are unchanged
colour.reference: mean, over HyperKvasir six-class frames without field flags, of each frame's in-field Lab mean and SD (fov crop at 224 px)

backbones.name: resnet50_gastronet_dino
backbones.source: GastroNet-5M DINOv1 ResNet-50 (portal access; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, frozen use only)

rq3.target: smallest k reaching 90% of the SAGE-only ceiling (macro-F1); report HyperKvasir + k above the ceiling as a finding

faithful.checkpoint: best weighted F1 on that test split
